chunks: Yaqub ibn Yusuf ibn Yaqub, the jurist and shaykh of the people of al-Rayy, narrated to us. He said: Ismail ibn Muhammad al-Saffar al-Baghdadi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ubayd ibn Utba al-Kindi narrated to us. He said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Sharik narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from al-A'mash from Ata. He said:
I asked Aisha about Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), and she said: That is the best of people; no one doubts regarding him except a disbeliever.

key_terms.خير البشر: The best of people/humankind -- a superlative title affirming Ali's supreme status
key_terms.كافر: Disbeliever -- one who denies a fundamental truth of faith

ai.seo_question: What did Aisha say about Ali ibn Abi Talib according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Ata reports that he asked Aisha about Ali ibn Abi Talib (as). She replied that Ali is the best of people, and no one doubts this except a disbeliever. This is part of a series of narrations in this assembly affirming the supreme virtue of Ali, with Aisha -- a prominent figure among the companions -- serving as the endorsing authority.
